A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNN solution-degeneracy study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments with independently trained RNNs on four tasks, including dynamical distances, weight distances, OOD variability, and intervention results.

after.justification: V2 reports original RNN experiments, including task-complexity, feature-learning, width, and regularization sweeps, with additional empirical analyses throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: V2 adds μP-style RNNs and a feature-learning control parameter γ, changing recurrent updates, initialization, readout scaling, and learning-rate scaling for the new interventions (Sections 3.3–3.4; Appendices G–H). Standard RNNs remain in other analyses. Auxiliary objectives and low-rank/sparsity regularization already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Both retain last-pulse memory, delayed amplitude discrimination, frequency-conditioned sine generation, and velocity-based 2D/3D navigation, with longer delays or trials for OOD evaluation. Delay manipulations and auxiliary outputs already appear in v1. V2's additional diagnostics and parameter interventions reuse this task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an empirical SVCCA comparison alongside the DSA-centered analysis, showing whether representational similarity follows the same trends (Appendix E, Figure 10). V1 has no corresponding evaluated comparison. V2's references to Procrustes and CKA comparisons describe prior work rather than additional original baseline experiments.

E3.justification: Behavioral degeneracy changes from coefficient of variation to standard deviation of OOD loss. Weight alignment changes from independent row/column permutations to a shared permutation. Fixed DSA ranks/delays are replaced by a reported PCA/full-rank protocol with lag selection over 1–30. Default flip-flop/path-integration width changes from 64 to 128, and several stopping thresholds change. V1's frequency-count sweep is omitted. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds memory-demand estimation, SVCCA analyses, OOD loss-distribution diagnostics, verification of feature-learning controls, and robustness checks using standard RNN parameterization (Appendices C, E–M). Regularization analyses extend beyond delayed discrimination to all four tasks. V1's entropy/PCA characterization and attractorness analysis are removed; example trajectories are retained elsewhere.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly identifies shaded bands and error bars as ±1 standard error, unlike v1's captions, and documents matched initializations across γ sweeps. Both versions already report 50 independently initialized networks per condition; an increase in that repeated-run count is not established.

E6.justification: V1's statement that changing delayed-discrimination delay leaves degeneracy invariant is replaced by decreasing dynamical/behavioral and increasing weight degeneracy in v2 Figure 4A. The dynamical width trend reverses under v2's μP setup. New γ results show reduced dynamical but increased weight and behavioral degeneracy (Figure 6). These are revised or newly reported findings under changed settings and metrics, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 removes the entropy-based task-complexity and attractorness definitions and substantively changes the permissible transformations in the weight-distance definition. Appendix H adds a change-of-variables derivation, credited to Miller and Fumarola, relating firing-rate model forms with matched inputs and initial conditions. These changes go beyond notation or standard metric explanations.

C1.justification: The claimed information-theoretic task-complexity contribution disappears. V2 centers its contributions on a four-factor double dissociation, introduces feature learning as a controlling factor, and replaces v1's size-increases-degeneracy discussion with a controlled-width decrease. Its abstract and introduction also acknowledge factor-dependent disagreement between behavioral and dynamical degeneracy.

C2.justification: V2 adds learning-regime explanations for weight dispersion and interprets increased OOD variability as possible overfitting. It explains competing width and feature-learning effects and discusses imperfect μP control, dynamical–behavioral decoupling, and the standard-RNN flip-flop exception (Discussion; Appendices F, J, M). V1's attractorness interpretation and delay-as-a-sloppy-dimension argument are removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies initialization and optimizer details, substantially expands path-generation parameters, documents μP scaling and task-specific time constants, and describes activation processing for DSA. It specifies the Procrustes package/function used for weight matching and adds hardware and compute accounting in Appendix N. These disclosures substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's tables.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around lazy/rich learning, NTK/μP, overparameterization, intrinsic dimension, and neural variability, while dropping the entropy-complexity comparison with Meister. The retained Contravariance Principle shifts from a consistency connection to a prominent claim of direct empirical validation. This exceeds bibliographic or citation-style updating.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Degeneracy definitions move into Methods, results are reorganized around controlling factors, and the standalone Related Work section disappears into the broader narrative. Task and training details are separated, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 adds an overview schematic, consolidates task schematics and retained example trajectories into Figure 2, and combines previously separate degeneracy displays in Figure 3. Auxiliary-loss attractor panels are reused in Figure 4. Entropy/PCA and attractorness displays disappear, numerous control/diagnostic plots are added, and Table 1 gains a behavioral column and revised factor organization.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's confounding of network width with learning regime through μP interventions and validation in Appendices I–M. OOD loss distributions and explicit dynamical–behavioral decoupling make its generalization interpretations more defensible. Removing entropy/attractorness analyses narrows scope, and width control remains imperfect for delayed discrimination, but the gains in experimental support, reproducibility, and qualification of the central conclusions are substantial.
